leads.Personalized Subject Line: The Dangerous Edge of Things and Deeper Than the Grave: an idea
leads.Personalized Email Body:
Hi Tina,

My name is Roland Jacobs. I'm a designer and book services specialist, helping authors professionally present, publish, and promote their books.

I came across The Dangerous Edge of Things and Deeper Than the Grave while researching your work. I was particularly interested in Tai Randolph's inherited Confederate-themed gun shop and a corpse in her brother's driveway in The Dangerous Edge of Things, and a tornado scattering remains at a Kennesaw Mountain cemetery in Deeper Than the Grave.

Those details gave me an idea for how customer retention could help present your books to more of the readers who may enjoy them. A reader-retention setup could guide people who finish one book straight to the next, with a reading-order page and a short follow-up sequence after each purchase.

I'd be happy to put together a complimentary concept sample so you can see the direction I have in mind.

Would you be open to taking a look?

Warm regards,
Roland Jacobs

leads.Personalized Subject Line: The Ruins and The Long Night: an idea
leads.Personalized Email Body:
Hi Steve,

My name is Roland Jacobs. I'm a designer and book services specialist, helping authors professionally present, publish, and promote their books.

I came across The Ruins and The Long Night while researching your work. I was particularly interested in a woman going alone to a German-speaking bar in 1954 Lindenhurst in The Ruins, and William L. Shirer's reporting on the rise of the Nazis in The Long Night.

Those details gave me an idea for how email marketing could help present your books to more of the readers who may enjoy them. A simple email setup (sign-up incentive, short welcome sequence, occasional updates) could keep readers who discover one book connected to the rest of your work.

I'd be happy to put together a complimentary concept sample so you can see the direction I have in mind.

Would you be open to taking a look?

Warm regards,
Roland Jacobs
